observed_defect: The original small log watchtower shows its roof edges without a clear readable timber support rhythm on the camera-facing front elevation; the left/front eave lacks foreground structural hierarchy.
design_intent: Add a modest three-part structural composition in dark, weathered timber on the front-facing left eave: a continuous fascia and two angled braces anchored visually against the log wall and toward the fascia. Protect the existing door, stairs, railings, roof tiles, UV atlas, and original mesh.
expected_visual_difference: From the fixed (6,-9,6) camera the upper front roofline should gain one visible horizontal dark-brown fascia and two diagonal wooden knee braces; the original tower keeps the same silhouette, roof shingles and stair access.

actions.reason: Visibly clarify the unsupported front eave edge with a long, slender timber fascia that does not interfere with stairs or the roof.
Use restrained weathered dark timber rather than masonry while leaving all inherited texture atlas slots untouched.
Add an angled physical timber knee brace supporting the left portion of the fascia from the solid upper log wall below.
Match the timber brace to the new dark fascia for a coherent unified architectural element.
Repeat the support language at the right end of the fascia with adequate clearance from the protected stair and railing system.
Match the second knee brace to the same timber material and keep the inherited atlas completely unchanged.
